observations: Three compact figures occupy a black ground, each with a round scribble-filled head showing bared teeth and yellow-circled eyes; the central figure is taller and more thickly layered with teal lines than the flanking two.
Orange and teal lines dominate the bodies, crossing and looping without closing into solid areas, while white outlines trace the outer silhouettes and red lines drift loosely behind the group.
A small red signature mark sits in the lower left; the background is pure black except for a multicolored striped wedge visible behind the left figure's shoulder.
reading: Three figures press together against a black void, their bodies built from crossing orange and teal lines that never close into solid form. Each round head carries bared teeth and yellow-ringed eyes, yet the three differ in scale and line density. The tight grouping and shared features invite a reading of kinship or mirroring, though the exposed teeth keep the mood unsettled.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors #12 and #14, both holding multiple open-mouthed figures. Where #12 spreads figures across a bright saturated field and #14 dissolves them into pale washes, #13 compresses them tightly against black.

connections.reason: nnxyz nnotb #12 shares the multi-figure bared-teeth format but spreads seven tall figures across a saturated color field rather than compressing three against black, making the spatial contrast direct and visible.
nnxyz nnotb #14 repeats the bared-teeth round heads and loose line bodies but dissolves them into a pale pink wash, showing the same figure vocabulary at the opposite end of the dark-to-light range.

lookingQuestion: The three figures share nearly identical head shapes and tooth marks — what differences in line density or color between them do you notice first?
ambiguities: The multicolored striped wedge behind the left figure's shoulder is partially obscured; its full extent is unclear from the image.
nnxyz nifty faces #0000 was inspected but its geometric, non-figure structure offered no useful formal connection to #13 and was omitted.
